excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<potuz0> Even if everything goes wrong and you never see any IL, what is the problem/complication that you are seeing? I am giving very concrete examples of advantages to decoupling them. There is one concrete advantage of coupling them that I see in that you can synchronously set the forkchoice node and you know that the IL was valid when you imported the block, other than that I see the list of advantages to decoupling vastly outweigh this: 
- Better pipelining (can use CPU and broadcast 10 seconds before your slot)
- Lighter blocks (you don't need to send the IL with them and you don't need to validate it at the same time as the payload)
- Better gossip validation (you do not need to enter the message to check that it was a block that you already imported) 
- Better Builder API (no changes) 

I would agree with you that falling back to RPC to request the IL would actually make me think twice, but if you don't I don't see how the list above is not contundent

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<potuz0> Since I don't follow let me rephrase in the sense that Franceso put it cause it's more readable: 

- A block comes, you do everything exactly as you do today, you import it and add it to forkchoice
- An IL comes you look/add for the node in forkchoice and add the il_present = true. 
- When calling get_head in forkchoice, it will filter out the leaves that don't have an IL. 

Your main concern was the fact that you couldn't consider the blocks valid until you had the blobs, this is no longer an issue here, blocks are valid, you can gossip them, act on them etc.. only thing is that get_head will filter out some leaves if they don't have a validated IL (re @InclusionList_bot: <tersec> there are a couple versions of "potuz's proposal":
- decoupled with validity for attesting (and sync committee too maybe) dependent on ILs every block, in time; and
- decoupled with validity for only proposing dependent on ILs this way

if I understand correctly?)
